design_condition: The low rectangular volume is set back from the rock and aligned with the existing school geometry, forming a generous shared courtyard while separating vehicle access from pedestrian outdoor areas.

positive.statement: The clear layout fits cleverly into the site and the geometry of the existing school.
The generous schoolyard accommodates the two basketball courts.
The low height preserves views toward the rock and village.
The setback accommodates a public path and a public square capable of hosting events.
The eastern vehicle access avoids traffic in the courtyard.
The three programs are arranged in a north-south row with separate entrances.
The common premises function as a buffer zone for the childhood-related program.
The crossing distribution area creates niches suitable for flexible use and small-group meetings.
The facades provide sheltered retreats appreciated in relation to the surroundings.
The separation between the gardens and the schoolyard is judicious.
The modular wooden construction integrates sustainability and allows a height extension.
The repetitive timber framework ensures good economy, controlled spans, and effective load transfer.
The structural choice is relevant given the weak soil and single-level construction.

negative.statement: The clear system seems rigid, and the cores between distribution spaces and activity rooms are questioned.
The three-entrance operation and the partitioning of the UAPE activity rooms are questioned by the user.
No response is given regarding the desired extension request.
